answer_summary.structure_k: K is heptakis-(2,6-anhydro)-beta-cyclodextrin (per-2,6-anhydro-beta-CD): TsCl (7 equiv = 1 per unit) tosylates only the primary 6-OH; NaOH then closes an intramolecular Williamson ether between O2 and C6 - the only trans-diaxial-competent closure (O3 can never attain the antiperiplanar geometry). Each unit therefore bears a 2,6-epoxide (2,6-anhydro) ring fused to the pyranose and retains exactly one free OH, at C3 (7 free OH in the whole molecule, as stated). Stereochemistry: all five stereocentres retain their geometry (SN2 occurs at C6, not a stereocentre); product CIP labels C1 S, C2 R, C3 R, C4 R, C5 R - the C2 S-to-R flip is purely a CIP re-ranking effect (O2 becomes a diether oxygen; the C3-side ring path outranks the C1-side path). On the answer template: bold new bond from C6 to O2 closing the five-membered 2,6-anhydro ring, single free -OH drawn at C3 (equatorial up), glycosidic alpha-1,4 stereobonds unchanged.
